title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions: Principal Values, Domains and Ranges
seo_title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions Class 12 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 2)
standard_text: Definition, range, domain, principal value branch; graphs of inverse trigonometric functions (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 12 Inverse Trigonometric Functions worksheet (NCERT Chapter 2): principal values of sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹, cot⁻¹, sec⁻¹ and cosec⁻¹, domains, ranges and expressions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The answer must lie in the principal value branch.
body_html:
How it works

  • Principal value branches: sin−1 [−π/2, π/2], cos−1 [0, π], tan−1 (−π/2, π/2), cot−1 (0, π), sec−1 [0, π] − {π/2}, cosec−1 [−π/2, π/2] − {0}.
  • Domains: sin−1 and cos−1 [−1, 1]; tan−1 and cot−1 R; sec−1 and cosec−1 R − (−1, 1).
  • sin−1(sin θ) = θ only if θ is in [−π/2, π/2]; otherwise find the angle in the branch with the same sine.
  • sin−1 x + cos−1 x = π/2 and tan−1 x + cot−1 x = π/2.
Example

Find the principal value of cos−1(−1/2).

cos(π/3) = 1/2

In [0, π], cos(π − π/3) = −1/2

Answer: 2π/3

Common mistakes

  • Giving −π/3 for cos⁻¹(−1/2) (it is outside [0, π]).
  • Writing sin⁻¹(sin 2π/3) = 2π/3.
  • Reading sin⁻¹ x as 1/sin x.

faq.q: Why is a principal value branch needed?
faq.a: sin x is not one-one on R, so its inverse needs a restricted range.

faq.q: Is sin⁻¹ x the same as (sin x)⁻¹?
faq.a: No. sin⁻¹ x is an angle; (sin x)⁻¹ = cosec x.

items.q: Find the principal value of cosec<sup>−1</sup>(−2/√3).
items.e: The principal branch of cosec−1 is [−π/2, π/2] − {0}. The angle there with cosec θ = −2/√3 is −π/3.

items.q: Find the principal value of sec<sup>−1</sup>(−2/√3).
items.e: The principal branch of sec−1 is [0, π] − {π/2}. The angle there with sec θ = −2/√3 is 5π/6.

items.q: Find the principal value of tan<sup>−1</sup>(1/√3).
items.e: The principal branch of tan−1 is (−π/2, π/2). The angle there with tan θ = 1/√3 is π/6.

items.q: Find the principal value of sec<sup>−1</sup>(2/√3).

items.q: Find the exact value of sin⁻¹(0).

items.q: Find the principal value of cot<sup>−1</sup>(1/√3).

items.q: What is the range of y = sin⁻¹ x?
items.e: Sine is restricted to the first and fourth quadrants so that it is one-one. −π/2 ≤ y ≤ π/2.

items.q: What is the domain of y = cos⁻¹ x?
items.e: The outputs of cosine are between −1 and 1, so those are the only inputs of cos⁻¹. −1 ≤ x ≤ 1.

items.q: What does sin⁻¹ x mean?
items.e: The −1 means inverse function, not a reciprocal. 1/sin x is csc x. The angle whose sine is x.

items.q: What is the range (principal value branch) of cos<sup>−1</sup>?
items.e: The principal value branch of cos−1 is [0, π].

c: Yes, because 32 is a real number
Yes, it equals 1 ÷ sin(32)
No, because 32 is not between −1 and 1
No, because 32 is not an angle
items.e: The domain of sin⁻¹ is −1 ≤ x ≤ 1, because sine and cosine are never outside that interval. No, because 32 is not between −1 and 1.

items.q: In which quadrants can the answer to sin⁻¹ x be?
items.e: The range of sin⁻¹ is −π/2 to π/2. the first and fourth quadrants.

items.q: Why must the domain of sine be restricted to define sin⁻¹?
c: Sine is not one-one, so it needs a piece where each output happens once
Sine is undefined for some angles
items.e: A function needs exactly one output for each input, so the inverse needs a one-one piece. Sine is not one-one, so it needs a piece where each output happens once.
